sketchMechanisms: The `object` declaration creates a singleton — exactly one instance can ever exist, and it is initialized lazily the first time it is accessed.
Optional chaining with `?.` — if any link in the chain is nil, the entire expression silently evaluates to nil without crashing.
Prolog's closed-world assumption: anything not provable from the knowledge base is considered false. An empty database answers every query with failure.
